intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Leaders react to Democratic midterm wins
items.text: Democrats took both the Senate and the House of Representatives in Tuesday's midterm elections. German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius called it a "historic victory". Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, described the result as a rejection of President Trump's policies. A UK minister, James Frith, called it a "seismic shift". China's foreign ministry spokeswoman, Mao Ning, said it was an internal American affair.

gloss.midterm elections: elections held halfway through a president's term
gloss.rejection: the act of saying no to something
gloss.seismic shift: a very big and sudden change
gloss.spokeswoman: a woman who speaks officially for a group or government
gloss.internal affair: a matter that only concerns one country

items.title: Trump says Iran war was worth the cost
items.text: President Donald Trump has said the war with Iran was worth the costs, even after his party lost the midterms. Asked if it was worth it, he replied, "I do. Yeah. I mean, well, you have no choice." He also said Vice President JD Vance was largely right that the war had cost Republicans seats, because it had pushed up petrol prices. Meanwhile, the Revolutionary Guard said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz.

gloss.worth the cost: valuable enough to justify what was spent or lost
gloss.push up: to make a price or number rise
gloss.tanker: a large ship that carries oil
gloss.strait: a narrow sea passage between two areas of land
gloss.party: a political group that competes in elections

items.title: Poundland jobs at risk as talks begin
items.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has asked Poundland's owners, Gordon Brothers, to find a practical solution to keep its shops open. Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds was due to meet them. Last week the company filed a notice of its intention to appoint administrators, which puts around 11,000 jobs at risk. Administrators are insolvency experts who take control of a failing business. The talks come as many high street retailers struggle with rising costs.

gloss.administrator: a person who takes control of a company that cannot pay its debts
gloss.file a notice: to formally send a document to an official body
gloss.high street: the main shopping street of a town
gloss.struggle with: to have great difficulty dealing with something

items.title: Fenerbahce beat Liverpool 3-2 in Istanbul
items.text: Fenerbahce came from behind twice to beat Liverpool 3-2 in the Champions League. Trey Nyoni put Liverpool ahead after 25 minutes, but Mason Greenwood levelled four minutes later. Alexander Isak restored the visitors' lead in the 69th minute. Archie Brown and Vedat Muric then scored within six minutes to win the match. It was Fenerbahce's first Champions League victory in more than 18 years.

gloss.come from behind: to win after losing at an earlier point
gloss.level: to score a goal that makes the score equal
gloss.within: inside a given period of time

items.title: Hijikata stuns Djokovic in Paris
items.text: Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata has beaten Novak Djokovic 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 in the second round of the Paris Masters. Djokovic won the first set but lost the next two. Elsewhere, Lorenzo Musetti knocked out top seed Alexander Zverev, while Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex Michelsen in two sets. Peruvian Ignacio Buse also beat fourth seed Daniil Medvedev.

gloss.qualifier: a player who won through early rounds to enter the main event
gloss.knock out: to defeat someone so they leave a competition
gloss.seed: a top player placed in a position to avoid other top players early
gloss.set: one part of a tennis match

items.title: Tiny supercurrent could read qubits safely
items.text: Researchers have proposed a new way to read quantum information without destroying it. At present, measuring a qubit usually damages its state. The team suggests detecting a tiny electrical signal, called a supercurrent, which comes from the qubit itself. If the idea works in experiments, it could make quantum computers more reliable. The study was reported by ScienceDaily this week.

gloss.qubit: the basic unit of information in a quantum computer
gloss.supercurrent: an electric current that flows with no resistance
gloss.propose: to suggest an idea or plan
gloss.reliable: able to be trusted to work well
gloss.state: the condition of something at a certain time

items.title: Viruses used against deadly superbugs
items.text: An international team has published the first joint guidelines for personalised phage therapy. Phages are viruses that infect and kill bacteria. Doctors hope they can treat infections that no longer respond to antibiotics. The guidelines aim to help hospitals use the treatment safely and consistently. Antibiotic resistance is a growing global health problem.

gloss.superbug: a bacterium that antibiotics can no longer kill
gloss.guidelines: official advice on how to do something
gloss.antibiotic resistance: when bacteria stop being killed by antibiotics
gloss.respond to: to react well to a treatment
gloss.aim to: to have something as a goal

items.title: Compound may help ageing muscles repair
items.text: Scientists have found a compound that changes a muscle-repair protein into a stronger version called Super HGF. The new form is more than twice as good at binding to its receptor, the part of a cell that receives the signal. The finding could one day help older people recover muscle after injury. The work is still at an early stage and has not yet been tested widely in people.

gloss.compound: a substance made of two or more chemical parts
gloss.protein: a substance in the body that does important jobs such as building muscle
gloss.receptor: a part of a cell that receives a chemical signal

items.title: BMW profit falls as 8,000 jobs go
items.text: BMW has reported that its pre-tax profit for the third quarter fell 11% to 2.08bn euros. The carmaker plans to cut about 8,000 jobs and has again lowered its forecast. In the UK, the Bank of England is expected to raise interest rates from 3.75% to 4% today. That would be its first rise in more than three years. On Wednesday the FTSE 100 closed up 1.8% at 10,829.21.

gloss.pre-tax profit: money a company makes before paying tax
gloss.forecast: a statement about what will probably happen
gloss.cut jobs: to remove jobs to save money
gloss.interest rate: the cost of borrowing money, shown as a percentage
gloss.close up: to end a day of trading at a higher price

items.title: GTA 6 preloading starts on 10 November
items.text: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto VI will launch on 19 November on PS5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X and S. Players who have pre-ordered the game can start preloading it from 10 November. The download is expected to need about 212GB of space. PlayStation has said it will share more information as the launch gets closer. Rockstar has confirmed the game is PS5 Pro Enhanced, but has not given details.

gloss.preload: to download a game before its official release
gloss.pre-order: to pay for a product before it is on sale
gloss.launch: the date when a product first goes on sale
gloss.enhanced: improved to work better on certain hardware
